subject: chemistry
title: Nitrogen and its compounds
key_idea: Nitrogen is unreactive because of its strong, non-polar triple bond. Ammonia is a Brønsted–Lowry base that forms the ammonium ion. Oxides of nitrogen cause smog and acid rain, and catalytic converters remove them from exhaust gases.

blocks.text: Nitrogen makes up most of the air yet reacts very little. This section covers why.

items: N₂ has a **triple bond**, N≡N. Its bond enthalpy is very large, about 944 kJ/mol.
A lot of energy is needed to break the bond, so the activation energy of its reactions is very high.
The molecule is **non-polar**, so polar reagents have no partial charge to attack.
Nitrogen reacts only under extreme conditions: lightning, hot engines or the Haber process.
The N≡N bond is very strong.
N₂ is non-polar, so it is not attacked by polar reagents.

blocks.text: Ammonia is a base, and it forms the ammonium ion. This section covers the basicity, the structure of NH₄⁺ and how ammonia is displaced from its salts.

items: Ammonia has a lone pair on N. It accepts a proton, so it is a **Brønsted–Lowry base**: NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺.
In water: NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻. The solution is weakly alkaline.
NH₃ reacts with acids to form ammonium salts: NH₃ + HCl → NH₄Cl.
In NH₄⁺, N forms four bonds in a tetrahedral shape, with bond angles of 109.5°.
One N–H bond is a **dative covalent bond**. Both electrons come from the lone pair on N.
The ammonium ion forms in an acid–base reaction, when ammonia accepts H⁺.
A stronger base removes H⁺ from NH₄⁺ and displaces ammonia: NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ → NH₃ + H₂O.
So warming an ammonium salt with sodium hydroxide gives off ammonia: NH₄Cl + NaOH → NaCl + NH₃ + H₂O.
This is also an acid–base reaction, because the ammonium ion acts as the acid.
Ammonia is a base because its lone pair accepts H⁺.
NH₄⁺ is tetrahedral and contains one dative bond.
A strong base such as OH⁻ displaces NH₃ from ammonium salts.

blocks.text: Nitrogen oxides form in several ways and cause pollution. This section covers their sources, their removal, smog and acid rain.

items: Lightning and hot engines give enough energy to break the N≡N bond: N₂ + O₂ → 2NO.
NO is oxidised in air to NO₂: 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂.
Natural sources include lightning and bacteria in soil. Man-made sources include car engines, power stations and aircraft.

diagram.alt: A sorting activity. Sort the sources of nitrogen oxides into natural and man-made.

items: A catalytic converter contains platinum, palladium and rhodium on a honeycomb.
It converts NO to N₂ and CO to CO₂: 2NO + 2CO → N₂ + 2CO₂.
Unburned hydrocarbons are also oxidised to CO₂ and H₂O.
NO and NO₂ react with unburned hydrocarbons in sunlight. They form **peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN)**, a component of photochemical smog.
NO₂ dissolves in rain to make nitric acid: 4NO₂ + O₂ + 2H₂O → 4HNO₃.
NO₂ also helps make sulfuric acid. It oxidises SO₂: NO₂ + SO₂ → NO + SO₃. Oxygen in air then regenerates the NO₂: 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂.
NO₂ is regenerated, so it acts as a catalyst. SO₃ then reacts with water: SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄.

diagram.alt: A loop showing NO₂ oxidising sulfur dioxide and being regenerated by oxygen.
steps: NO is oxidised back to NO₂ by O₂
SO₃ dissolves in rain to form H₂SO₄

items: NO forms where there is enough energy to break N≡N, and NO₂ forms from NO and oxygen.
Catalytic converters change NO and CO into N₂ and CO₂.
NO₂ forms acid rain directly and acts as a catalyst in making sulfuric acid.
